sources.title: When RLVR Shrinks the Reasoning Boundary: Diagnosing Pass@k Inversion
sources.note: Pass@k inversion is a useful diagnostic of RLVR mode coverage and rare correct trajectories, with PBA reducing boundary losses under matched GRPO. It concerns offline policy post-training and sampling coverage rather than autonomous persistent self-modification at deployment.

sources.title: LOGOS: A Living Logic for AI Agent Teams That Evolve With Humans
sources.note: LOGOS is strong governance evidence for self-evolving agent systems: prompts, memory, skills, tools, roles, and workflows remain isolated release candidates until held-out execution evidence, human-owned policy, and authorization permit promotion. Gate ablations show off/proxy rules can adopt harmful candidates while evidence gates reject them in controlled suites. This strongly supports the Research-OS authority, evidence, rollback, and release-engineering boundary, but it is a governance/control protocol rather than a newly identified irreducible scientific self-evolution variable.

sources.title: Toward Auditable AI Scientists: A Hypothesis Evolution Protocol for LLM Agents
sources.note: HEP makes hypotheses persistent typed objects with unique ids, append-only event logs, belief updates, lifecycle states, explicit tests, evidence attachment, refinement, and merging. Compared with a planning-style agent it produces a much more explicit hypothesis-test-evidence-belief cycle. This is high-value Research-OS component evidence for auditable scientific reasoning and hypothesis state, but it does not establish a new causal self-evolution object beyond structured scientific state and workflow.

sources.title: Scoped Verification for Reliable Long-Horizon Agentic Context Evolution under Distribution Shift
sources.note: GRACE is the strongest r7 near-boundary source. It holds model, tools, harness, initial instruction, experience batches, held-out evaluation set, and batch-level update schedule fixed, and compares flat-text HCE, a graph substrate without structural analysis, and full graph-regularized scoped validation under alternating distribution shift. Full GRACE sustains strict reliability while flat text and graph-without-consolidation degrade, strongly supporting structural representation plus local validation/consolidation for long-lived control artifacts. However the treatments differ in representation and the semantic information available to the update/validation procedure; internal LLM-call budgets are not matched and diagnosis content can diverge after the first update. If full typed graph/executable instruction semantics are supplied to the strongest versioned/nonstationary/context-maintenance baseline, the result is an implementation/verification advantage rather than an additional causal state variable. Preserve as a watch seed for a same-semantic-content, same-compute representation test.

reopen_contracts_checked.boundary: A strongest versioned/nonstationary treatment baseline must receive the full observable instruction semantics, graph relations, version state, and update history; GRACE does not show an opposite ex-ante prediction after that information parity.

Failure-derived instruction edits and consolidation remain corrective context/skill optimization once failure evidence, semantic content, edit budget, update count, and held-out evaluation are matched.

sources.title: Religion and Artificial Intelligence as Distributed Meaning Systems: A Naturalistic Conceptual Model
sources.note: This source is a conceptual comparison of religion and AI as distributed meaning systems. It provides no execution-backed intervention on an autonomous agent and the optional full text was unavailable in this refresh, so it is outside the scientific self-evolution gate.

sources.title: Mach-Mind-4-Flash Technical Report
sources.note: Mach-Mind-4-Flash is a multi-stage foundation-model post-training report using domain RL experts, distillation, and token-efficiency optimization. The deployed model is fixed rather than autonomously evolving across tasks.

sources.title: WCog-VLA: A Dual-Level World-Cognitive Vision-Language-Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
sources.note: WCog-VLA is an end-to-end driving architecture with semantic and generative world modeling. Its world evolution is predicted environment/trajectory state within inference, not persistent improvement of the agent artifact.

sources.title: AutoPersonas: A Multi-Timescale Loop Engine for Open-Ended Persona Evolution
sources.note: AutoPersonas documents a real long-run self-locking symptom in recursive persona-life loops and shows a same-runtime A/B where context-slice masking plus per-sample divergence targeting substantially reduces macro-theme repetition while the downstream OSO absorption chain remains active. But the intervention explicitly changes what historical/state context the generator can see and injects withheld divergence targets, so it changes pre-outcome information and sampling pressure rather than isolating a hidden self-evolution variable. The paper itself states that it lacks a scalar co-evolution metric, broad persona coverage, and exhaustive component ablation. The current result therefore reduces to context gravity/visibility, diversity-seeking generation, and evidence-governed state management.

reopen_contracts_checked.boundary: The compared systems do not have identical pre-outcome information because masking changes visible state/history and divergence targeting changes the generation objective; no same-information residual beyond information/proxy/distribution effects is isolated.

sources.title: Single-Rollout Asynchronous Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
sources.note: SAO is an asynchronous RL post-training algorithm designed for stability and off-policy correction. It is an optimization/training method, not deployment-time persistent self-evolution.

sources.title: Onnes: A Physics-Grounded Multi-Agent LLM Simulator for Cryogenic Fault Diagnosis in Quantum Computing Infrastructure
sources.note: Onnes is a physics-grounded simulator and multi-agent diagnosis study. The improved panel recovers with curated few-shot demonstrations and self-consistency without parameter updates; this is in-context scaffolding over a simulated diagnostic task, not persistent autonomous self-modification.

sources.title: From Intent to Infrastructure: LLM-Driven Agent Compilers for ISAC Networks
sources.note: The ISAC Agent Compiler provides a verifiable policy-graph intermediate representation and separates fast parameter control, subgraph recompilation, and full workflow recompilation across time scales. This is useful systems/control-plane evidence for hierarchical runtime adaptation and recompilation, but the reported mechanism is explicit engineering control over an infrastructure configuration rather than an irreducible agent self-evolution causal state.

sources.title: CurateEvo: Data-Curation Evolving for Agentic Post-Training
sources.note: CurateEvo explicitly represents the data-curation strategy as executable code and evolves it from failed held-out-development trajectories. At each epoch the strategy transforms the same fixed raw corpus into SFT data, RL data, and an inference-time memory bank; the agent is retrained from the same base with a fixed recipe and evaluated on a fixed dev set. Ablations show effectiveness-driven revision is the largest contributor and each output resource helps. This is a clean verifier-guided program/data-pipeline search over an explicit objective, with ordinary failure-driven corrective adaptation and selection on a development proxy; it does not identify a new self-evolution causal primitive.

reopen_contracts_checked.boundary: Executable curation-code generation, execution, evaluation, and revision are expressible as verifier-guided program search/repair when the strongest baseline receives the same raw corpus, failure transcript, candidate code, objective, and search budget.
Failed-dev-trajectory-driven revisions remain corrective adaptation after matching failure evidence, supervision, update budget, and held-out evaluation.

sources.title: Turning Off-Policy Tokens On-Policy: A Plug-in Approach for Improving LLM Alignment
sources.note: SIS is a token-level importance-sampling correction for RL post-training. It improves training stability and performance but does not define a persistent autonomous deployment-time update process.

sources.title: Multiplayer Interactive World Models with Representation Autoencoders
sources.note: This multiplayer world model predicts a shared dynamic environment under several agents actions. The optional full text was unavailable in this refresh; the abstract describes a fixed learned simulator rather than an autonomous self-evolving agent artifact.

sources.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier: A General-Purpose Verification Framework
sources.note: LLM-as-a-Verifier supplies fine-grained continuous verification signals by scoring token-logit expectations and scaling through repeated evaluation and criteria decomposition; it can also serve as a dense RL reward. This is strong evaluator/control-plane component evidence, but the verifier itself is not a longitudinal self-evolution scientific object.

sources.title: KAT-Coder-V2.5 Technical Report
sources.note: KAT-Coder-V2.5 is an agentic model post-training stack built from reconstructed executable environments, filtered trajectories, RL, and expert distillation. The final model is fixed at deployment and does not instantiate autonomous persistent self-evolution.
